summary: Created Kubernetes deployment manifests for all services with production-grade configuration
reason_for_change: No Kubernetes manifests existed for production deployment. Docker Compose only supports single-node development. Production requires MongoDB replica set, Redis HA, horizontal scaling, and proper service discovery.
implementation_details: Created comprehensive K8s manifests including: (1) Namespaces for prod/staging/dev isolation, (2) Secrets for sensitive configuration, (3) MongoDB StatefulSet with 3-node replica set and init job, (4) Redis deployment with persistence, (5) Backend deployment with HPA, (6) Celery worker deployment with queue-based autoscaling, (7) Frontend deployment with HPA, (8) NGINX Ingress with TLS via cert-manager, (9) PodDisruptionBudgets for all critical services, (10) ServiceMonitors for Prometheus scraping, (11) Alert rules for monitoring.
architecture_impact: Enables production deployment with horizontal scaling, fault tolerance, and proper service isolation
security_impact: TLS termination, network policies ready via ingress annotations, secrets managed via K8s secrets
performance_impact: HPA enables automatic scaling based on CPU/memory and queue depth
database_impact: MongoDB replica set provides fault tolerance with automatic failover
backward_compatibility: No code changes required - same internal URLs used
migration_requirements: Deploy to K8s cluster. MongoDB replica set requires keyfile secret. cert-manager must be installed.
evidence: k8s/ directory contains 9 YAML files covering all production services. Replica set configuration in mongodb.yaml. HPA in backend.yaml and celery-worker.yaml.
known_risks: MongoDB init job may fail if pods not ready. Redis sentinel may need additional configuration for master election.
rollback_plan: kubectl delete -f k8s/ removes all manifests. Retain old Docker Compose for fallback.
